newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher after CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher after CPI.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Sunday after the release of a lower-than-expected April consumer price index (CPI), traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.66 percent, or 1.73 points, to 265.84 on all-share turnover of 115 million shekels against 160 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.71 percent higher at 273.27.
The April CPI, released after the end of the trading day on Thursday, rose 0.7 percent, lower than market expectations of a rise of 1.1 percent.

"The relatively low CPI was the main reason for today's rise but the market is rising very slowly. It's difficult to predict where the market is going in the coming days and it is facing a test at the current level," said Yossi Weidelfeld at Eyal Securities.

"The market made a nice move during the last few weeks and the lower-than-expected CPI is another indicator supporting the positive trend," said Jacques Goldhar, head of International Activities at Jerusalem Capital Markets.
Weidelfeld said that in the long term the market will continue to rise. "The trend is positive but in the short term everything is possible," he said.
"The CPI together with other economic indicators will put more pressure on the Bank of Israel to lower its key lending rate," Goldhar said.
The central bank last cut its key rate at the end of February to 13.9 percent.
"I believe that we will see a moderate rate cut of less than 0.5 percentage points this month," Weidelfeld said.
Goldhar added that another indicator supporting the positive mood is that the market is rising with growing volume.

Bank Leumi, the most active share, rose 3.0 percent to 530 agorot on volume of 7.3 million shekels. The head of MI Holdings, the Israeli government agency charged with selling state-owned banks, said on Sunday a European road-show to woo investors for a share offering of Bank Leumi was sucessful.
Discount Investments rose 3.75 percent to 28,803 agorot. The company said on Sunday that earnings per share for the first quarter of 1997 rose to 7.1 shekels from 5.9 shekels a year earlier.

Delek, the Israel Fuel Corp, gained 2.25 percent to 10,534 agorot. Delek said on Sunday that net profit in the first quarter rose to 42.8 million shekels from 29.8 million shekels at the same quarter last year.

Other active share include Bank Discount which gained 1.25 percent to 368 agorot on turnover of 5.8 million shekels and Bezeq Israel Telecom, which rose 0.5 percent to 870 agorot on volume of 5.4 million shekels.
